title: Git: first-time setup & auth
intro: One-time configuration on a new machine, plus connecting to GitHub with a token or SSH key.

blocks.p:
git config sets configuration options.

--global makes this apply to all repositories on your computer.

user.name is the name that shows on commits.

user.email is the email linked to your GitHub account.
blocks.code:
Git uses these to record who made each commit.

git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "youremail@example.com"

blocks.h: Set your default code editor (optional but recommended)
blocks.p:
core.editor tells Git which editor to open when it needs you to type messages.

"code --wait" tells Git to wait until you close VS Code before continuing.

You can replace code with nano, vim, etc., if you prefer.

blocks.h: Starting from scratch on your computer
Copying an existing project from GitHub
Use HTTPS with a personal access token (PAT) instead of your password.
blocks.p:
Go to GitHub → Settings → Developer Settings → Personal Access Tokens → Generate new token.

Give it repo permissions.

Use the token instead of your password when Git asks.
Copy the public key (~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub) to GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys.
